lessons.title: MIST, ATMIST & SBAR: High-Fidelity Handover
lessons.summary: handover ที่ดีถ่ายทอด trajectory, severity และสิ่งที่ต้องทำต่อ—not a data dump.

sections.title: 1) MIST/ATMIST
paragraphs: Age/Time/Mechanism/Medical complaint, Injuries/Information, Signs including trends, Treatments and response.

sections.title: 2) SBAR
paragraphs: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation works well for interprofessional escalation and structured updates.

sections.title: 3) Trends matter
paragraphs: “BP 90/60” น้อยกว่าการบอก “120/80 → 90/60 despite 500 mL; HR rising 100→130.” Include response to treatment.

sections.title: 4) Closed-loop
paragraphs: Pause for questions and explicitly hand over responsibility, drugs running, airway/device status and unresolved risks.

lessons.title: Emergency Medical Dispatch: From Call to Safe Resource Allocation
lessons.summary: dispatch decisions shape care before ambulance arrival through structured interrogation, prioritization and caller instructions.

sections.title: 1) Core tasks
paragraphs: Identify location/callback, chief complaint, immediate threats, consciousness/breathing and scene hazards; assign priority/resource according to system protocol.

sections.title: 2) Caller instructions
paragraphs: High-impact pre-arrival instructions include CPR/AED, hemorrhage control, childbirth support and airway positioning when protocol allows. Keep instructions simple and verify understanding.

sections.title: 3) Dynamic incidents
paragraphs: Update responding crews with meaningful changes: arrest, violence, entrapment, number of patients, hazardous material or need for additional agencies.

sections.title: 4) Quality
paragraphs: Dispatch QA reviews protocol compliance, under/over-triage, caller comprehension and outcome-linked opportunities—not only call duration.

lessons.title: Mass Casualty Incident: Triage, Command & Resource Matching
lessons.summary: เมื่อ demand เกิน resources เป้าหมายเปลี่ยนจาก individual optimization เป็น greatest good with organized command.

sections.title: 1) Scene organization
paragraphs: Safety, incident command, zones, communication, casualty collection and transport coordination prevent chaos.

sections.title: 2) Triage
paragraphs: Use your jurisdiction’s MCI triage system consistently; categories prioritize immediate threat, delayed care, minor injury and expectant/deceased according to policy.

sections.title: 3) Re-triage
paragraphs: Triage category can change after treatment or deterioration. Reassess at collection/transport points.

sections.title: 4) Distribution
paragraphs: Avoid overwhelming the nearest hospital; coordinate destination based on capacity and specialty.

lessons.title: Interfacility Transfer & Critical Transport
lessons.summary: transport is a clinical procedure: anticipate what can fail when moving away from the current resources.

sections.title: 1) Stabilize and define purpose
paragraphs: Know why the patient is moving, receiving capability, transport time and what cannot be provided en route.

sections.title: 2) Device/medication check
paragraphs: Airway secure, oxygen reserve, ventilator battery, IV lines, pumps, drains, blood products and medication supply must cover transport with margin.

sections.title: 3) Risk forecast
paragraphs: Ask: what is most likely to deteriorate in the next hour? Prepare rescue drugs/equipment and thresholds for intervention.

sections.title: 4) Documentation/handover
paragraphs: Include baseline and latest trends, imaging/labs, allergies, medications, procedures, response, pending tasks and accepting clinician/facility.

lessons.title: EMS Documentation, Clinical Reasoning & QA
lessons.summary: PCR should reconstruct what happened, why decisions were made and how the patient changed.

sections.title: 1) Narrative structure
paragraphs: Dispatch/scene → initial impression/primary survey → focused history/exam → serial vitals → interventions with dose/time → response → consultation → transport/handover.

sections.title: 2) Objective language
paragraphs: Document observed facts and patient statements. Avoid judgmental labels; describe behavior/mental status.

sections.title: 3) Trends and response
paragraphs: Serial data is stronger than isolated values. Record failed attempts, complications and corrective actions.

sections.title: 4) QA value
paragraphs: Good records support continuity, audit, education and system improvement. Missing timestamps/doses/device confirmation can hide safety problems.
